says: The Process object's alarm handler lets a runner failure escape and never sets the alarm again, so after the platform's six retries a program's saved wake is dropped until some other call reaches the object; decision 0105 says an alarm handler catches its own failures and always re-arms.
proof: runtime.ts:858-861 is rpc(storage.get('wake')) then runner.due(at), with no catch. Runner.ts:1286 sets alarmAt = undefined before the work (the platform consumed the alarm), and setAlarm runs only on the paths that return (Runner.ts:1409, catchUp's publish at :878); a LedgerError from ready(), mailbox.send (:1414-1420) or the refused branch (:1418) leaves storage 'wake' set and no alarm. Cloudflare's base class docs: alarm() 'will be retried upon failure using exponential backoff, starting at two second delays for up to six retries'. No test in next/ fails an alarm seven times.
cost: A program that asked to wake later silently never wakes if the ledger or storage fails for about two minutes around its due time; nothing records that the wake was missed.
